| [CLAIM-378](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-378.md) v2 | Linear-invariant similarity sees column space | The generalization of [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md)'s theorem. If col(X) = col(Y), write X = BC and Y = BD with B a basis of the common column space and C, D of full row rank, extend C and D to invertible matrices, and the quotient maps X onto Y. Since XA always has the column space of X, the GL(p) orbits are exactly the sets of n × p matrices sharing a column space. Theorem 1 is the case of column space ℝⁿ. Column-centred matrices of rank n − 1 all have column space 1^⊥, so an invariant index cannot tell them apart either. | Active |

| [CLAIM-382](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) v2 | Autoencoder representations are rotation-invariant | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. Transform the parameters by orthogonal maps Q_l of the hidden spaces that commute with the activation. The network then computes Q_l h_l and the same output, so the loss is invariant. Gradient steps commute with the transformation, and an i.i.d. Gaussian initialisation is invariant under it, so the law of the trained representations is too. For radial activations this is all of O(n), and no basis is privileged in law. For elementwise ones it is a finite group, so the axes may be privileged. Whether they are, and how strongly, is [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s empirical content. The argument needs an orthogonally equivariant optimiser, and fails for Adam. | Active |

Every attribute is read out exactly, by an affine map, from the full-rank spectral embedding, and the recovered incidence and its concept lattice equal the generating ones. What implication changes is the spectrum. On a balanced b-ary tree, the eigenvectors are branch contrasts rather than one per attribute. A branching at depth ℓ gives eigenvalue μ_ℓ = w Σ_{ℓ′>ℓ} λ_ℓ′ b^(D−ℓ′), with multiplicity (b−1)bˡ, and these fall strictly with depth for any positive strengths. So a rank-(b^K − 1) embedding reads out exactly the attributes of depth at most K. Below the cut, each attribute's readout is the same constant on every descendant of its depth-K ancestor, so siblings merge. Along a tree, PMI additivity is therefore the same thing as piecewise constancy on the finest groups: it has content only where attributes cross-cut, as in analogy families. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

Items then have equal norms and inner products that depend only on the depth of their common ancestor, so any kernel of inner products and norms is a sum of block matrices that act as a scalar μ_ℓ on each level: [K, P_ℓ] = 0 exactly, A2's Conjecture A condition holding by symmetry. Kernel flow from zero output then gives each level's risk as exp(−2μ_ℓt/N), and μ_ℓ depends on c alone: target strengths never enter the order. For a decoupled, balanced deep linear network the same data give T_ℓ/T_m → c_m g_m / c_ℓ g_ℓ as the initial scale goes to zero (the [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) solution with diagonal input covariance). So the same data can be coarse-first for one learner and simultaneous or fine-first for the other, and in neither does the tree's depth set the order. The commutator ‖[A, P_ℓ]‖ is exactly the coupling between level ℓ and the rest. Against the flow under Σ P_ℓ A P_ℓ, in which no level talks to another, level ℓ's relative residual departs by at most ‖[A, P_ℓ]‖/(λ_ℓ s_ℓ) at any time, λ_ℓ being the level's slowest rate and s_ℓ its share of the initial residual; the constant cannot be improved. It follows that each acquisition time lies in an interval, that the symmetric order survives any perturbation of the operator below a threshold proportional to the rate gap, and that below a risk of about that ratio squared the slowest mode sets every level's time, so the times converge in ratio.
